data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports Chile’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). For Chile, the factsheet reports a mean creative thinking score of 31/60, significantly below the OECD average (33), and provides proficiency-level distributions (74% at Level 3+; 20% at Level 5–6). It also reports associations with mathematics and reading performance (correlations of 0.61 and 0.58) and variance decomposition (29% uniquely explained by mathematics). The document is descriptive and comparative; it does not specify an ML modeling approach, PV handling, or missing-data procedure for an analysis conducted within the factsheet.
